$schema_note: Machine-readable companion to context/crosswalks/framework-crosswalk.md. The markdown carries the nuance; this file carries the mappings for tooling (scripts/crosswalk_query.py, the MCP server). Domain-level navigation aid ONLY: cells point to the control area most relevant to each domain, not clause-by-clause equivalence — never present output built from this file as a compliance mapping deliverable. Ranges use 'A.5.1-A.5.8' form (both ends share a prefix and differ in the trailing number). Every domain name here must appear as a row in the markdown tables — the validator enforces name-level sync.
$verification: Reflects public framework texts as of mid-2026; verify against official sources (CIS mappings, NIST OLIR, AICPA, PCI SSC) before relying on a mapping. Last reviewed: 2026-07.

iso27001.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A
iso27001.id_style: Annex A controls per ISO/IEC 27002:2022, e.g. A.5.15

soc2.name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
soc2.id_style: common criteria CC1-CC9 and category criteria A/C/PI/P, e.g. CC6.1, A1.2

sp80053.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
sp80053.id_style: two-letter families and controls, e.g. AC, AC-4

domains.name: Governance & risk management

iso27001.notes: Plus ISMS clauses 4-10, which Annex A crosswalks miss

csf2.notes: GV: all categories — the strongest governance articulation of the six

cis8.notes: No dedicated control; policy/process expectations embedded per safeguard (v8.1 adds governance emphasis)

domains.friction: When assessing governance maturity, do not rely on a CIS- or PCI-anchored control set alone — both treat governance thinly.

domains.name: Asset management

soc2.notes: Partial; no dedicated inventory criterion — auditors typically test under CC6.1

domains.friction: SOC 2 has no dedicated inventory criterion; PCI v4 made scope/asset inventory explicit.

domains.name: Access control & identity
domains.friction: The cleanest row in the crosswalk, but fine-grained differences remain large (e.g. PCI Req 8 MFA specifics vs ISO A.8.5 outcome-level wording).

domains.name: Physical & environmental

cis8.notes: Not covered — CIS v8 deliberately excludes physical security

domains.friction: If CIS is your primary framework, source physical controls from ISO A.7 or 800-53 PE.

domains.name: Continuity & resilience

soc2.notes: A-series applies only when Availability is in scope

pcidss4.notes: Not directly addressed (incident response plan aside)

domains.friction: SOC 2 covers continuity only if Availability is in scope; PCI barely addresses it.

domains.name: Logging & monitoring
domains.friction: Frameworks split logging vs monitoring vs detection differently — map at safeguard level before claiming coverage.

domains.name: Vulnerability & threat management
domains.friction: Granularity differs by an order of magnitude: ISO has a single control (A.8.8); PCI prescribes scan cadence, ASV scans, and pen testing.

derived_frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC 2.0
derived_frameworks.note: 800-171 derives from 800-53; use the 800-53 column, then narrow to CUI scope

derived_frameworks.name: FedRAMP
derived_frameworks.note: 800-53 r5 baselines plus FedRAMP-specific parameters — the 800-53 column applies directly

derived_frameworks.name: HITRUST CSF
derived_frameworks.note: Ships its own authoritative-source mappings; prefer those over this table

derived_frameworks.name: CSA CCM v4
derived_frameworks.note: Cloud-specific domains (IPY, SEF) have no clean single parent; map at safeguard level

derived_frameworks.name: COBIT 2019
derived_frameworks.note: IT governance wrapper, not a security control catalog — expect thin coverage below the governance row

derived_frameworks.name: NERC CIP
derived_frameworks.note: Sector-mandatory; its own asset-categorization logic (CIP-002) drives everything

derived_frameworks.name: ISO 22301
derived_frameworks.note: Full BCMS behind the continuity row's ISO A.5.29-A.5.30 cells

derived_frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27701
derived_frameworks.note: Adds privacy (PIMS) controls on the 27001 machinery

derived_frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 42001
derived_frameworks.note: AI-specific obligations mostly sit outside these security domains

derived_frameworks.name: NIST AI RMF
derived_frameworks.note: AI-specific obligations mostly sit outside these security domains

derived_frameworks.name: ACSC Essential Eight
derived_frameworks.note: Eight prioritized mitigations, closest to CIS safeguards; no governance layer

derived_frameworks.name: TISAX
derived_frameworks.note: VDA ISA catalogue follows 27001/27002 structure with automotive additions
